newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis banks Mercantile, Mark Twain, to merge.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis banks Mercantile, Mark Twain, to merge.

text.p: Mercantile Bancorp Inc. and Mark Twain Bancshares Inc., bank holding companies based in St. Louis, said Monday they agreed to merge in a deal valued at $855 million.
The transaction was structured as a tax-free exchange of shares, they said.

The addition of Mark Twain, a bank holding company with $3.1 billion in assets, and its 39 locations in the St. Louis and Kansas City, Mo., areas will strengthen Mercantile's presence in the three largest Missouri markets. Mercantile has $18.2 billion in assets.

Under the terms of the agreement, Mark Twain shareholders will receive 0.9520 share of Mercantile common stock for each share of Mark Twain common stock, the banks said. Based on Friday's closing price of $52.125 for Mercantile's common stock, the transaction is valued at $49.62 per share of Mark Twain, they said.
Mark Twain's shares, which closed Friday at $42.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, jumped $4.125 to $46.50 in early trading Monday. Mercantile's fell $1.50 to $50.625, also on the NYSE.
Upon completion of the merger, Alvin Siteman, chairman of Mark Twain Bancshares, will become chairman of Mercantile Bank of St. Louis, and join the Mercantile Bancorp board.

John Dubinsky, president and chief executive of Mark Twain Bancshares, will become president and chief executive of Mercantile Bank of St. Louis and a member of Mercantile's management executive committee.
Both men will report to Mercantile Bancorp Chairman and Chief Executive Thomas Jacobsen.

Mercantile Bankcorp operates banks in Missouri, Iowa, Kansas, Illinois and Arkansas. Mercantile's non-banking subsidiaries include companies providing brokerage services, asset-based lending, investment advisory services, leasing services and credit life insurance.

"This merger ... brings together the strengths of two high-performing organisations and solidifies Mercantile's position as the largest locally managed, and independently owned banking operation in St. Louis and the state of Missouri," Jacobsen said in a statement announcing the agreement.
Plans call for the merger to be completed in the second quarter of 1997, subject to the approval of Mercantile and Mark Twain shareholders and all appropriate regulatory agencies, the companies said.
Mercantile has mergers pending with Today's Bancorp, Inc., First Financial Corporation of America, and Regional Bancshares, Inc.
